name: Zanzibar Beaches
tagline: White-sand beaches, turquoise water and dhows on a tropical spice island.
highlight: Watching the tide drift out and a dhow sail past at sunset on a quiet beach.
shortDescription: The north and east coast beaches of Zanzibar: Nungwi, Kendwa, Paje, Jambiani, Matemwe and Michamvi, plus snorkelling, kite-surfing and red colobus monkeys.
metaDescription: Zanzibar beaches guide: Nungwi, Kendwa, Paje, Jambiani, Matemwe, tides, snorkelling, kitesurfing, Jozani forest, where to stay, costs and a four-day plan.
nearestAirport: Abeid Amani Karume International (ZNZ), 45-90 minutes by road

image.alt: A white sandy beach at Nungwi, Zanzibar

intro: Zanzibar is ringed by white sand and clear water, and the choice of beach comes down to tides and mood. The north (Nungwi and Kendwa) has swimmable water all day and a livelier scene, while the east coast (Paje, Jambiani, Matemwe, Michamvi) is quieter, with dramatic tides that pull the sea far out.

Beyond sunbathing there is plenty to do: snorkelling and diving on the reefs, kitesurfing at Paje, dhow cruises, dolphin trips at Kizimkazi and seaweed farming visits with local women. The Jozani Chwaka Bay forest is the home of the rare Zanzibar red colobus monkey.

Pick one or two bases rather than moving every night. Travel on the island is by taxi or minibus, and the northern and eastern coasts are about an hour from Stone Town. It is a mainly Muslim island, so cover up away from the beach resorts.

whyVisit.intro: Zanzibar offers the classic Indian Ocean beach holiday, with culture on the side.

gettingThere.intro: Most visitors arrive via Stone Town or the airport.

gettingAround.intro: Taxis and minibuses link the coasts.

bestTime.headline: June-October
bestTime.summary: Dry season brings sun and cooler breezes, with the best conditions for snorkelling.
bestTime.avoid: April and May, when rains close some lodges.

itinerary.title: Four days on the Zanzibar coast
itinerary.intro: A mix of beach and activity.

tips: Check tide tables, since east coast swimming is tide-dependent.
Book dive and boat trips with licensed operators.
Avoid peak season if you can.

faq.a: Nungwi for swimming, Paje for kiting.
